title: CS25 Fourier pair-identity = the LineIncidence spectral identity = the Gauss-period sup-norm M(n), via the SAME dual-code Parseval
evidence: Two probes in scripts/probes/_407_conn/ (exact-arithmetic / numpy, proper dyadic mu_n < F_q*, q=1 mod n, q~n^4, n=8/16/32/64, multiple primes). (1) probe_C020_parseval_identity.py PART A numerically confirms CS25 fourier_pair_identity (LHS=85=RHS, err=0); it is already an axiom-clean Lean lemma (CS25FourierIdentity.lean: fourier_pair_identity), as is the line-incidence side (LineIncidenceSpectral.lean: lineIncidence_spectral, charSum_l2_pairing). (2) The structural identification is CORRECT and verified: the per-surviving-frequency coefficient is exactly the Gauss-period sum C(b)=sum_{x in mu_n} e_p(b x), and its worst over b!=0 is exactly M(n) (probe_C020_crosscone_offdiag.py: direct |C(b*)| == M(n), match=True at every (n,q)). So F2/F3/F16/F18 genuinely share ONE spectral vector {C(b)}. (3) THE DISCRIMINATING FACT: CS25 only delivers the L2 functional sum_b |C(b)|^2, which equals q*n EXACTLY for every prime (Parseval, charSum_l2_pairing) -- regime-independent and free. The prize needs the L-inf functional M(n)=max_{b!=0}|C(b)|, which is provably NOT a function of the L2 mass: at fixed n=16 three primes all have L2 mass q*n but M(n)=13.84/13.30/13.93 (different). The gap sqrt(L2)/M(n) = 24,74,252,850 grows like sqrt(q) (the square-root loss). M(n)/sqrt(n log(p/n)) is the bounded-but-drifting open constant 1.07->1.20->1.26->1.36 (matches the grounding §5 measurements).
reduced_to: Bound the WORST surviving dual frequency in the CS25/line-incidence off-diagonal, i.e. M(n)=max_{b!=0 mod p}|sum_{x in mu_n} e_p(b x)| for proper dyadic mu_n < F_q* (the L-inf functional of the shared spectral vector). The connection rigorously identifies CS25's off-diagonal, LineIncidenceSpectral, and the Gauss-period sup-norm as ONE Parseval object and EXPLAINS why CS25 only reaches Johnson (it controls L2 = free, discards the L-inf worst term). It supplies a proven bridge: any future M(n) <= C*sqrt(n log(p/n)) feeds CS25's E[N^2] through the in-tree axiom-clean identities. But it gives no new bound on M(n).
wall: W-BGK (square-root cancellation of incomplete character sums over thin multiplicative subgroups = the generalized-Paley non-principal eigenvalue / Paley Graph Conjecture). The L2-to-Linf gap is the W4/large-sieve sqrt-loss (sqrt(L2)/M ~ sqrt(q)); restricting Parseval mass to one frequency is exactly the open core.
honest_note: PROVEN sub-part: both Lean lemmas are in tree and axiom-clean, and the per-frequency coefficient = Gauss-period sum, worst = M(n), is exact (probe match=True). The cross-cone identification (F2/F3/F16/F18 = one shared spectral vector via the same dual-code Parseval) is CORRECT and is a genuine insight that explains the Johnson barrier. NOT closed: the connection is an identity of objects plus an explanation, not a bound. It welds the prize residual back to bounding M(n) = W-BGK, the recognized 25-year-open problem. No closure claimed. The CS25 off-diagonal being the open research kernel is already noted in DISPROOF_LOG.md (lines ~1783-1801, 'the sharp bound on THIS is exactly the CS25/#82 research kernel'); this attack adds the precise per-frequency = M(n) identification and the L2-determines-nothing demonstration. The proposed Lean lemma cs25_fourier_offdiag_eq_lineIncidence_spectralError was NOT built (it is a clean rewrite between two existing axiom-clean lemmas and would be a real PROVEN bridge, but it does not affect the OPEN status of M(n)); time-boxed to probes.
